text:
elaine: Quick bug: our sample-app live demo crashed yesterday during an org-level key rotation. The app was a containerized background worker using `REDWOOD_API_KEY` from the env. It failed with intermittent 401s but kept running.

jon: envs are inherited at process start; they don't magically update. Did you mount the key from a file or bake it into the image?

elaine: we mount `/etc/creds/redwood.key` into the container and set `REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /etc/creds/redwood.key)` in the unit file. Ops rotated the key in the host file, but the container's process still had the old value.

priya: for containers, best pattern is to have the process read from a credential provider or a file at intervals, or signal it to reload. Recommending two options in docs: 1) run a tiny sidecar credential agent that serves the current key over a unix socket; 2) support `SIGHUP` to re-read `/etc/creds/redwood.key`.

sam: FYI the JS SDK already has a `credentialProvider` hook used by cloud functions. The CLI doesn't. We should unify the chain: CLI / SDKs / sample apps -> credential provider -> fallback to env -> fallback to file -> metadata. That makes rotation atomic.

elaine: can we add a small shim script in our onboarding repo that demonstrates a systemd + container example? Many folks copy/paste and assume `export` will update running containers.

jon: also add a log line on auth failure that indicates the source checked (e.g. `auth tried: env,file,provider`) without printing keys. Helps debugging.

priya: agreed. small API suggestion: credential provider should expose `get()` and an optional `watch(callback)` that triggers when creds change. That avoids polling.

sam: open question: project vs org scoping. If a process had an org-scoped key and a new project-scoped key is issued, what should precedence be for long-lived processes? For safety I'd prefer newest key override irrespective of scope, but we must surface a warning when scope narrows.

elaine: add `REDWOOD_PROJECT` and `REDWOOD_ORG` env vars to samples and mention that project-scoped keys will restrict access. Also add a note in tutorials: rotating to a narrower scope requires ensuring the worker only needs that scope.

infra-bot: image-scan: sample-app:v2 promoted @ 2025-07-14T18:03:00Z

jon: next steps: 1) small CLI PR to include credential provider hook + SIGHUP reload for `rw stream`; 2) add sample-app sidecar example in onboarding repo; 3) docs update for env precedence and container rotation patterns. I'll file tickets and tag @priya @sam.

elaine: thanks — i'll update the sample-app README with the systemd + docker examples and call out the `REDWOOD_PROJECT` var.

priya: +1. also add a test-case in the SDK integration tests that rotates a key file mid-process to validate no silent 401s.

sam: cool. i'll draft the credential-provider minimal spec and share in the RFC channel.
